note: The 239 wrong headlines reported by acid tester 1 (false matches), 14 Nov 2026: each was run through the collectors' own matchers on main and was attached to the project named. 'real' marks the seven headlines found published (with their link); the others are test wording. 'matched_by' and 'confidence_given' are what main did; 'rule_classes' names the matching rule at fault.

rule_classes.W0: core scored weakness 0 by trade.weakness() (two or more words, not all in COMMON), so the bare phrase in any feed headline matches with no solar word; every Planning Resource and Construction Enquirer feed headline is tested against all 200 projects
rule_classes.ADJ: trade ADJACENT allows up to two arbitrary words between the core and 'solar'/'energy', so another site or another subject followed by 'solar' passes as 'solar or energy word directly after it'
rule_classes.CTY: one-word core (weakness 1) accepted with the county or planning-authority word anywhere in the title; no solar word needed
rule_classes.GEN: the alias is a generic farm/lane/place name followed by 'Solar Farm'; the full alias in the title is accepted by all three matchers with no second agreeing fact
rule_classes.IDXW: index weak rule: core and 'solar' anywhere in the title, kept as weak (uncertain) but still published
rule_classes.IDXADJ: index adjacency rule: core directly followed by 'solar' counts as strong even when the next words are 'panels', 'cell' or 'canopy'
rule_classes.DEV: the agreeing 'developer' term is the first operator token outside OPERATOR_STOP, here an everyday word matched case-insensitively anywhere in the title
rule_classes.DUP: two of the 200 projects share this core, so one headline attaches to both
rule_classes.FOREIGN: the full alias contains 'solar', so official.match and index.match_item accept it anywhere in the title; neither applies a foreign-place filter and none needs a second term
